symptom: A catalog query removes the text `Catalog.` even inside a string literal, so a module named Catalog cannot be filtered on: `select QualifiedName, 'Catalog.Product' as lit from CATALOG.ENTITIES` returns lit = 'Product', and `... where QualifiedName = 'Catalog.Product'` returns 0 rows although the entity exists. Reported for `mxcli -c`; the same on exec scripts, the REPL and the LSP (which shells out to -c). Siblings of the same rewrite: a quoted identifier `"Catalog.Name"` and comments were rewritten too, and `CATALOG . ENTITIES` (whitespace at the dot, which the grammar accepts) failed with `no such table: CATALOG.ENTITIES`.
cause: execCatalogQuery stripped the prefix with a case-insensitive regex `\bcatalog\.([a-z_][a-z0-9_]*)` over the raw query text, which cannot tell a table reference from data. The mode warning beside it had the same flaw in a second textual scan: it took the word after the first `from ` in the text, so a literal containing 'from' hid the real table and only the first table of a join was ever checked.
file: `mdl/executor/catalog_query_rewrite.go` (`rewriteCatalogTableRefs`, a SQLite-shaped token scanner), `mdl/executor/cmd_catalog.go` (`execCatalogQuery`, `warnIfCatalogModeInsufficient` now takes the scanner's table list; `extractTableFromQuery` removed); tests `mdl/executor/cmd_catalog_prefix_rewrite_test.go`; repro `mdl-examples/bug-tests/catalog-1450-prefix-in-string-literals.mdl`
insight: There is exactly one place user SQL meets the catalog (MDL SELECT -> visitor extractOriginalText -> execCatalogQuery); -c, scripts, the REPL and the LSP all reach it, and Starlark lint exposes builtins, not raw SQL, so one fix covers every path. Rewriting SQL text needs a lexer, not a regex: skip single-quoted strings (doubled-quote escape), double-quoted/backtick/bracket identifiers and both comment forms, and treat `catalog` as the prefix only when it is a whole identifier token followed by a dot and a name, not preceded by a dot. Follow SQLite's lexing, not MDL's: the text goes to SQLite verbatim. An ATTACHed `catalog` schema would have avoided rewriting altogether, but the catalog is an in-memory SQLite DB, which cannot be attached to itself without changing how it is opened. Let the warning consume the tables the scanner found, so the rewrite and the warning cannot disagree about which tables a query reads. Revert proof: 19 subtests fail on the old regex (the issue's two queries, literals, quoted identifiers, comments, whitespace at the dot, the warning cases); the controls (upper/lower/mixed prefix, joins, subqueries, ProductCatalog.Item / my_catalog aliases) pass both ways.
